<PubmedArticle><MedlineCitation Status="MEDLINE" Owner="NLM" IndexingMethod="Automated"><PMID Version="1">41621206</PMID><DateCompleted><Year>2026</Year><Month>07</Month><Day>06</Day></DateCompleted><DateRevised><Year>2026</Year><Month>07</Month><Day>06</Day></DateRevised><Article PubModel="Print-Electronic"><Journal><ISSN IssnType="Electronic">1879-2782</ISSN><JournalIssue CitedMedium="Internet"><Volume>199</Volume><PubDate><Year>2026</Year><Month>Jul</Month></PubDate></JournalIssue><Title>Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society</Title><ISOAbbreviation>Neural Netw</ISOAbbreviation></Journal><ArticleTitle>Matrix-Transformation based Low-Rank Adaptation (MTLoRA): A brain-inspired method for parameter-efficient fine-tuning.</ArticleTitle><Pagination><StartPage>108642</StartPage><MedlinePgn>108642</MedlinePgn></Pagination><ELocationID EIdType="doi" ValidYN="Y">10.1016/j.neunet.2026.108642</ELocationID><ELocationID EIdType="pii" ValidYN="Y">S0893-6080(26)00104-8</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText>Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) reduces the compute and memory demands of adapting large language models, yet standard low-rank adapters (e.g., LoRA) can lag full fine-tuning in performance and stability because they restrict updates to a fixed rank-r subspace. We propose Matrix-Transformation based Low-Rank Adaptation (MTLoRA), a brain-inspired extension that inserts a learnable r&#x202f;&#xd7;&#x202f;r transformation T into the low-rank update (&#x394;W=BTA). By endowing the subspace with data-adapted geometry (e.g., rotations, scalings, and shears), MTLoRA reparameterizes the rank-r hypothesis class, improving its conditioning and inductive bias at negligible O(r<sup>2</sup>) overhead, and recovers LoRA when T=I<sub>r</sub>. We instantiate four structures for T-SHIM (T=C), ICFM (T=CC<sup>&#x22a4;</sup>), CTCM (T=CD), and DTSM (T=C+D)-providing complementary inductive biases (change of basis, PSD metric, staged mixing, dual superposition). An optimization analysis shows that T acts as a learned preconditioner within the subspace, yielding spectral-norm step-size bounds and operator-norm variance contraction that stabilize training. Empirically, MTLoRA delivers consistent gains while preserving PEFT efficiency: on GLUE (General Language Understanding Evaluation) with DeBERTaV3-base, MTLoRA improves the average over LoRA by (+2.0) points (86.9&#x202f;&#x2192;&#x202f;88.9) and matches AdaLoRA (88.9) without any pruning schedule; on natural language generation with GPT-2 Medium, it raises BLEU on DART by (+0.95) and on WebNLG by (+0.56); and in multimodal instruction tuning with LLaVA-1.5-7B, DTSM attains the best average (69.91) with &#x202f;&#x223c;&#x202f;4.7% trainable parameters, outperforming full fine-tuning and strong PEFT baselines. These results indicate that learning geometry inside the low-rank subspace improves both effectiveness and stability, making MTLoRA a practical, plug-compatible alternative to LoRA for large-model fine-tuning.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>Copyright &#xa9; 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
